objective: Publish independently audited one-edge failure tolerance, unique optimal hub-link restoration, and a dominated-upgrade counterexample in the specified multipartite family, with portable exact certificates.
evaluator_command:
uv run --project experiments/kemeny-one-deletion-proof --frozen python experiments/kemeny-one-deletion-proof/verify_certificate.py --certificate experiments/kemeny-one-deletion-proof/symbolic.json --output work/kemeny-one-deletion-proof/check-01.json
uv run --project experiments/kemeny-one-deletion-proof --frozen python experiments/kemeny-one-deletion-proof/verify_all_deletions.py --certificates experiments/kemeny-one-deletion-proof/all-deletions --output work/kemeny-one-deletion-proof/all-deletions-01.json
uv run --project experiments/kemeny-one-deletion-proof --frozen python experiments/kemeny-one-deletion-proof/verify_optimal_repair.py --certificate experiments/kemeny-one-deletion-proof/optimal-repair.json --output work/kemeny-one-deletion-proof/optimal-repair-01.json

claims.statement: Spectral K formulas, twin quotient reductions, and ordinary edge-deletion updates are published tools; they are not claimed as new methods.
Six deletion representatives exhaust nine labeled endpoint categories; the determinant ratio and zero-mode correction also cover a=3.
All six reconstructed deletion ratios equal their complete positive numerator and denominator certificates.
For integers 3<=a<=b,c, every original-edge deletion f in G=K_(a,b,c) join K1 leaves K(G-f+uv)<K(G-f) for any pair u,v in its selected minimum part.
Five missing-edge orbits exhaust the hub-damaged graph; split-endpoint determinant ratios retain the correct n-m correction in comparing interventions.
All five optimal-repair comparison ratios match complete positive numerator and denominator certificates.
For H=G-uh in the specified minimum-part domain, restoring uh is the unique minimum-K single missing-edge insertion; an untouched A pair also strictly beats uv.
At a=b=c=3, uv is worse than an untouched A insertion by exactly 17/17856, independently verified from full matrices.
Restoring the specified failed hub link strictly improves K relative to the damaged graph.

checks.note: All public copies/artifacts/claim locators checked; canonical results equal independent replays and rc0 raw output.
Full endpoint/tie/a3 domain; exactly one original deletion; optimal restoration admissible and unique; alternate A not globally ranked.
Direct primary passages support only known-method attributions; novelty and practical impact excluded.
Unchanged independently audited implementations/results and corrected final prose align; CI static only until push.

limitations: Global originality, publication priority, Lean formalization, and measured real-world benefit remain unresolved.
Exactly three non-singleton parts of sizes at least three and one hub; exactly one original-edge failure. No weighted or multi-failure extension.
Optimal repair assumes the specific minimum-part hub-link failure and that restoration is an admissible unit-weight edge insertion. The best non-restoration alternative is not fully ranked.
Historical attempt failures, local environment paths, explicit recovery-cap amendment and author/reviewer status statements are retained unchanged. The portable package is the fresh-checkout route.
Published methods are reused. Bounded and sometimes weak literature retrieval cannot certify novelty.
Workflow has static review at assembly; actual GitHub execution must be retained separately after push.
